Category.Name: Application Profiles
Category.Description: Application level profiles represent a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Application. They specifically include Transport Profiles and generally also Security Profiles.

Category.Name: Server
Category.Description: Profiles of this category specify functions of an OPC UA Server. The URI of such Profiles can be exposed in the Server capabilities.

Category.Name: Client
Category.Description: Profiles of this category specify functions of an OPC UA Client.

Category.Name: Publisher
Category.Description: Profiles of this category specify functions of an OPC UA Publisher.

Category.Name: Subscriber
Category.Description: Profiles of this category specify functions of an OPC UA Subscriber.

Category.Name: Transport
Category.Description: Profiles of this category specify specific protocol mappings. The URI of such Profiles has to be part of an Endpoint Description.

Category.Name: Security
Category.Description: Profiles of this category specify security related functions. Security policies are part of this category. The URI of Client-Server security policies has to be part of an Endpoint Description returned from the GetEndpoints Service.

Category.Name: Global Directory Service
Category.Description: Profiles of this category specify functions for global discovery and certificate management.

Category.Name: Miscellaneous
Category.Description: Profiles of this category do not have any other suitable category.

Profile.Name: A & C Acknowledgeable Alarm 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support for Acknowledgement of active Conditions. This Facet builds upon the A&C Base Condition Server Facet. Acknowledgement requires support of the Acknowledge Method and the Acknowledged state. Support of the Confirmed state and the Confirm Method is optional. This Facet supersedes the A & C Acknowledgeable Alarm Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Address Space Instance 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support required for a Server to expose Alarms and Conditions in its AddressSpace. This includes the A & C AddressSpace information model. This Facet supersedes the A & C Address Space Instance Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Address Space Instance Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use Condition instances in the AddressSpace.

Profile.Name: A & C Alarm 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support for Alarms. Alarms extend the AcknowledgeableConditionType by adding an Active state which indicates when something in the system requires attention by an Operator. This Facet builds upon the A & C Acknowledgeable Alarm Server Facet. This facet requires that discrete AlarmTypes be supported, it also allows for optional support of shelving, alarm comments and other discrete AlarmTypes such as Trip or Off-Normal. This Facet supersedes the A & C Alarm Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Alarm Auditing Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that Audit Events are generated for Alarms. All optional Conformance Units are mandatory if the corresponding feature is supported; e.g., "A & C Latching Auditing" is mandatory if "A & C Latched State" in the "A & C Alarm Server Facet" is supported.

Profile.Name: A & C Alarm Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the alarming model (the AlarmType or any of the sub-types).

Profile.Name: A & C AlarmMetrics Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the AlarmMetrics model, i.e. understand and use the collected alarm metrics at any level in the HasNotifier hierarchy.

Profile.Name: A & C AlarmMetrics Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support for AlarmMetrics. AlarmMetrics expose status and potential issues in the alarm system. A Server can provide these metrics at various levels (operator station, plant area, overall system etc.).

Profile.Name: A & C Base Condition 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires basic support for Conditions. Information about Conditions is provided through Event notifications and thus this Facet builds upon the Standard Event Subscription Server Facet. Conditions that are in an “interesting” state (as defined by the Server) can be refreshed using the Refresh Method. Optionally the server may also provide support for Condition classes. This Facet supersedes the A & C Base Condition Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Base Condition Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the Alarm and Condition basic model. This includes the ability to subscribe for Events and to initiate a Refresh Method.

Profile.Name: A & C CertificateExpiration 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support of the CertificateExpirationAlarmType. It is used to inform Clients when the Server’s Certificate is within the defined expiration period. This Facet supersedes the A & C CertificateExpiration Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C CertificateExpiration Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the CertificateExpirationAlarmType.

Profile.Name: A & C Dialog 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support of Dialog Conditions. This Facet builds upon the A & C BaseCondition Server Facet Dialogs are ConditionTypes used to request user input. They are typically used when a Server has entered some state that requires intervention by a Client. For example, a Server monitoring a paper machine indicates that a roll of paper has been wound and is ready for inspection. The Server would activate a Dialog Condition indicating to the user that an inspection is required. Once the inspection has taken place the user responds by informing the Server of an accepted or unaccepted inspection allowing the process to continue. This Facet supersedes the A & C Dialog Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Dialog Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the dialog model. This implies the support of Method invocation to respond to dialog messages.

Profile.Name: A & C Enable 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires the enabling and disabling of Conditions. This Facet builds upon the A&C Base Condition Server Facet. Enabling and disabling also requires that instances of these ConditionTypes exist in the AddressSpace since the enable Method can only be invoked on an instance of the Condition. This Facet supersedes the A & C Enable Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Enable Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to enable and disable Alarms.

Profile.Name: A & C Exclusive Alarming 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support for Alarms with multiple sub-states that identify different limit Conditions. This facet builds upon the A&C Alarm Server Facet. The term exclusive means only one sub-state can be active at a time. For example, a temperature exceeds the HighHigh limit the associated exclusive LevelAlarm will be in the HighHigh sub-state and not in the High sub-state. This Facet requires that a Server support at least one of the optional Alarm models: Limit, RateOfChange or Deviation. This Facet supersedes the A & C Exclusive Alarming Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Exclusive Alarming Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the exclusive Alarm model. This includes understanding the various subtypes such as ExclusiveRateOfChangeAlarm, ExclusiveLevelAlarm and ExclusiveDeviationAlarm.

Profile.Name: A & C Non-Exclusive Alarming 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support for Alarms with multiple sub-states that identify different limit Conditions. This Facet builds upon the A&C Alarm Server Facet. The term non-exclusive means more than one sub-state can be active at a time. For example, if a temperature exceeds the HighHigh limit the associated non-exclusive LevelAlarm will be in both the High and the HighHigh sub-state. This Facet requires that a server support at least one of the optional alarm models: Limit, RateOfChange or Deviation. This Facet supersedes the A & C Non-Exclusive Alarming Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Non-Exclusive Alarming Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the non-exclusive Alarm model. This includes understanding the various subtypes such as NonExclusiveRateOfChangeAlarm, NonExclusiveLevelAlarm and NonExclusiveDeviationAlarm.

Profile.Name: A & C Previous Instances 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support for Conditions with previous states that still require action on the part of the operator. This Facet builds upon the A&C Base Condition Server Facet. A common use case for this Facet is a safety critical system that requires that all Alarms be acknowledged even if it the original problem goes away and the Alarm returns to the inactive state. In these cases, the previous state with active Alarm is still reported by the Server until the Operator acknowledges it. When a Condition has previous states it will produce events with different Branch identifiers. When previous state no longer needs attention the branch will disappear. This Facet supersedes the A & C Previous Instances Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Previous Instances Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use previous instances of Alarms. This implies the ability to understand branchIds.

Profile.Name: A & C Refresh2 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet enhances the A & C Base Condition Server Facet with support of the ConditionRefresh2 Method. This Facet supersedes the A & C Refresh2 Server Facet.

Profile.Name: A & C Refresh2 Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet enhances the A & C Base Condition Server Facet with the ability to initiate a ConditionRefresh2 Method.

Profile.Name: A & E Proxy Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet describes the functionality used by a default A & E Client proxy. A Client exposes this Facet so that a Server may be able to better understand the commands that are being issued by the Client, since this Facet indicates that the Client is an A&E Com Client.

Profile.Name: A & E Wrapper 2022 Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the requirements for a UA Server that wraps an OPC Alarm & Event (AE) Server (COM). This Profile identifies the sub-set of the UA Alarm & Condition model which is provided by the COM OPC AE specification. It is intended to provide guidance to developers who are creating servers that front end existing applications. It is important to note that some OPC A&E COM Servers may not support all of the functionality provided by an OPC UA A&C server, in these cases similar functionality maybe available via some non-OPC interface. For example if an A&E COM server does not support sending Alarm Acknowledgement messages to the system that it is obtaining alarm information from, this functionality may be available via some out of scope features in the underlying Alarm system. Another possibility is that the underlying system does not require acknowledgements or automatically acknowledges the alarm. It supersedes the A & E Wrapper Facet.

Profile.Name: Access Token Request Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the use of the RequestAccessToken Method on an Authorization Server (defined in UA Part 12) to request such a token.

Profile.Name: Address Space Notifier Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires the support of a hierarchy of Object Nodes that are notifiers and Nodes that are event sources. The hierarchy is commonly used as a way to organize a plant into areas that can be managed by different operators.

Profile.Name: AddressSpace Lookup Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to navigate through the AddressSpace and includes basic AddressSpace concepts, view and browse functionality and simple attribute read functionality.

Profile.Name: Advanced Type Programming Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the type model and process the instance AddressSpace based on the type model. For example a client may contain generic displays that are based on a type, in that they contain a relative path from some main type. On call up this main type is matched to an instance and all of display items are resolved based on the provided type model.

Profile.Name: Aggregate Subscriber Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the aggregate filter when subscribing for Attribute values.

Profile.Name: Aggregate Subscription 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the handling of the aggregate filter when subscribing for Attribute values. This Facet supersedes the Aggregate Subscription Server Facet.

Profile.Name: AliasName Aggregating Server Facet
Profile.Description: Defines the use of AliasNames in an aggregating Server.

Profile.Name: AliasName Client Facet
Profile.Description: Defines the use of AliasNames in a Client.

Profile.Name: AliasName Configuration Facet
Profile.Description: Defines the functionality related to configuration of AliasNames

Profile.Name: AliasName Server Facet
Profile.Description: Defines the use of AliasNames in a Server.

Profile.Name: AliasName Server PubSub Publisher Facet
Profile.Description: Supports the publication of AliasName changes via the PubSub notifications

Profile.Name: Attribute Read Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read Attribute values of Nodes.

Profile.Name: Attribute Write Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to write Attribute values of Nodes.

Profile.Name: Attribute WriteMask Server 2023 Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the capability to update characteristics of individual Nodes in the AddressSpace by allowing writing to Node Attributes. It requires support for authenticating user access as well as providing information related to access rights in the AddressSpace and actually restricting the access rights as described.

Profile.Name: Attribute WriteMask Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the capability to update characteristics of individual Nodes in the AddressSpace by allowing writing to Node Attributes. It requires support for authenticating user access as well as providing information related to access rights in the AddressSpace and actually restricting the access rights as described. [Note: in the future this Facet will be Deprecated and replaced by "Attribute WriteMask Server 2023 Facet"]

Profile.Name: Auditing 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires the support of Auditing which includes the Standard Event Subscription Server Facet. Support of this Facet requires that Audit Events be produced when a Client performs some action to change the state of the Server, such as changing the AddressSpace, inserting or updating a value etc. The auditEntryId passed by the Client is a field contained in every Audit Event and allows actions to be traced across multiple systems. The Audit Event Types and their fields shall be exposed in the Server’s AddressSpace. This Facet supersedes the Auditing Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Auditing Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to monitor Audit Events.

Profile.Name: Authorization Service Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the support for configuring the necessary information to validate access tokens when presented by a Client during session establishment. Access Tokens are issued by Authorization Services.

Profile.Name: Base Client Behaviour Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet indicates that the Client supports behaviour that Clients shall follow for best use by operators and administrators. They include allowing configuration of an endpoint for a server without using the discovery service set; Support for manual security setting configuration and behaviour with regard to security issues; support for Automatic reconnection to a disconnected server. These behaviours can only be tested in a TestLab. They are best practice guidelines.

Profile.Name: Base Event Processing Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to subscribe for and process basic OPC UA Events. The Client has to support at least one of the Events in the Facet.

Profile.Name: Base Historical Event 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the server requirements to support basic Historical Event functionality, including simple filtering and general access. This Facet supersedes the Base Historical Event Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Base Server Behaviour Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines best practices for the configuration and management of Servers when they are deployed in a production environment. It provides the ability to enable or disable certain protocols and to configure the Discovery Server and specify where this Server shall be registered.

Profile.Name: Best Practice – Administrative Access
Profile.Description: The Server and Client allow restricting the use of certain Services and access to parts of the AddressSpace to administrative personnel. This includes multiple level of administrative access on platforms that support multiple administrative roles (such as Windows or Linux).

Profile.Name: Best Practice – Alarm Handling
Profile.Description: A Server should restrict critical alarm handling functionality to users that have the appropriate rights to perform these actions.

Profile.Name: Best Practice – Audit Events
Profile.Description: Subscriptions for Audit Events shall be restricted to authorized personnel.

Profile.Name: Best Practice – Audit Events Client
Profile.Description: Audit Tracking system connect to a Server using a Secure Channel and under the appropriate authorization to allow access to Audit Events.

Profile.Name: Best Practice – Random Numbers
Profile.Description: All random numbers that are required for security should use appropriate cryptographic library based random number generators.

Profile.Name: Best Practice – Strict Message Handling
Profile.Description: Server and Client reject messages that are incorrectly formed as specified in UA Part 4 and UA Part 6.

Profile.Name: Best Practice – Timeouts
Profile.Description: The administrator should be able to configure reasonable timeouts for Secure Channels, Sessions and Subscriptions. Setting these timeouts allows limiting Denial of Service attacks and overload issues.

Profile.Name: Client Redundancy Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the Server actions that are required for support of redundant Clients. Support of this Facet requires the implementation of the TransferSubscriptions Service which allows the transfer of Subscriptions from one Client’s Session to another Client’s Session.

Profile.Name: ComplexType 2017 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet describes the support of Variables with enumerated and or structured DataTypes. The Read, Write and Subscriptions service set shall support the encoding and decoding of these structured DataTypes. As an option the Server can also support alternate encodings, such as an XML encoding when the binary protocol is currently used and vice-versa.

Profile.Name: Core 2022 Client Facet
Profile.Description:
This Facet defines the core functionality required for any Client. It includes the core functions for Security and Session handling.
It supersedes the Core 2017 Client Facet.

Profile.Name: Core 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description:
This Facet defines the core functionality required for any UA Server implementation. The core functionality includes the ability to discover endpoints, establish secure communication channels, create Sessions, browse the AddressSpace and read and/or write to Attributes of Nodes. The key requirements are: support for minimum one Session, support for the core AddressSpace structure, and the Server Capabilities Object, and authentication with UserName and Password. For broad applicability, it is recommended that Servers support multiple transport and security Profiles.
It supersedes the Core 2017 Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Data Access Quantities Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support for the DataAccess Quantity Model. It requires exposing of QuantityType instances and ServerUnitType instances.

Profile.Name: Data Access Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support for an Information Model used to provide industrial automation data. This model defines standard structures for analog and discrete data items and their quality of service. This Facet extends the Core Server Facet which includes support of the basic AddressSpace behaviour.

Profile.Name: DataAccess Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to utilize the DataAccess Information Model, i.e., industrial automation data like analog and discrete data items and their quality of service.

Profile.Name: DataChange Subscriber 2022 Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to monitor Attribute values for data change.

Profile.Name: Diagnostic Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read and process diagnostic information that is part of the OPC UA information model.

Profile.Name: Dictionary Reference Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support of Dictionary References to relate Nodes in the AddressSpace to external dictionaries.

Profile.Name: Discovery Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to discover Servers and their Endpoints.

Profile.Name: Documentation – Client
Profile.Description: This Facet provides a list of user documentation that a Client application should provide.

Profile.Name: Documentation Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines a list of user documentation that a server application should provide.

Profile.Name: Durable Subscription 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies support of durable storage of data and events even when Clients are disconnected. This Facet implies support of any of the DataChange or Event Subscription Facets.

Profile.Name: Durable Subscription Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies use of durable Subscriptions. It implies support of any of the DataChange or Event Subscriber Facets.

Profile.Name: Embedded 2022 UA Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application for devices with more than 50 MBs of memory and a more powerful processor. This Profile builds upon the Micro Embedded Device Server Profile. Besides various enhancements, this Profile requires that Servers expose OPC-UA types in the AddressSpace.
This Profile supersedes the Embedded 2017 UA Server Profile.

Profile.Name: Embedded 2025 UA Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application for devices with more than 50 MBs of memory and a more powerful processor. This Profile builds upon the Micro Embedded Device Server Profile. Besides various enhancements, this Profile requires that Servers expose OPC-UA types in the AddressSpace.
This Profile supersedes the Embedded 2022 UA Server Profile.

Profile.Name: Embedded DataChange Subscription 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the minimum level of support for data change notifications within subscriptions. It minimizes memory and processing overhead required to implement the Facet. This Facet includes functionality to create, modify and delete Subscriptions and to add, modify and remove Monitored Items. It is recommended that Servers shall support one Subscription with up to two items for each Session. In addition, support for two parallel Publish requests is suggested. This Facet is geared for a platform such as the Nano or Micro Embedded Device Server Profiles in which memory is limited and will be managed. It supersedes the Embedded DataChange Subscription Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Enhanced DataChange Subscription 2017 Server Facet
Profile.Description:
Note: This Facet has been deprecated in v1.05, because it only adds limits and in 1.05 we require limits to be described in the product documentation.

This Facet specifies an enhanced support of subscribing to data changes. It is part of the Standard UA Server 2017 Profile. This Facet increases the limits defined by the Standard Data Change Subscription 2017 Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Entry Level Support 2015 Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to interoperate with low-end Servers, in particular Servers that support the Nano Embedded Profile but in general Servers with defined limits.

Profile.Name: Event Subscriber Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to subscribe for Event Notifications. This includes basic AddressSpace concept and the browsing of it, adding events and event filters as monitored items and adding subscriptions.

Profile.Name: Exposes Type System Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to expose meta data in the AddressSpace, i.e. data that describe the various OPC UA Types used by the Server. Note that each Node defined in the core specification parts has ConformanceUnits defined that require the Node to be in the AddressSpace. If a Server supports such a ConformanceUnit, it shall expose the Nodes related to the ConformanceUnit in its AddressSpace.

Profile.Name: File Access Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use File transfer via the defined FileType. This includes reading and optionally writing.

Profile.Name: File Access Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support of exposing File information via the defined FileType. This includes reading of file as well as optionally writing of file data.

Profile.Name: GDS AliasName Server Facet
Profile.Description: Defines the use of AliasNames in a GDS.

Profile.Name: Global Certificate Management Client 2022 Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Client Application that uses the Push Model for the global management of Certificates and Trust Lists.
This Profile supersedes the Global Certificate Management Client 2017 Profile".

Profile.Name: Global Certificate Management Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the capability to interact with a Global Certificate Management Server to obtain an initial or renewed Certificate and Trust Lists.

Profile.Name: Global Certificate Management Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the capability to interact with a Global Certificate Management Server to obtain an initial or renewed Certificate and Trust Lists.

Profile.Name: Global Discovery and Certificate Mgmt 2022 Server
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application. that acts as a global discovery server and a global certificate manager.
This Profile supersedes the Global Discovery and Certificate Management 2017 Server.

Profile.Name: Global Discovery Client Facet
Profile.Description: Support of this Facet enables system-wide discovery of Servers using a Global Discovery Server (GDS).

Profile.Name: Global Discovery Server 2022 Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application that acts as a global discovery server.
This Profile supersedes the Global Discovery Server 2017 Profile.

Profile.Name: Global Service Authorization Request Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the capability of a Server (like a GDS) to provide access tokes to OPC UA Clients via an Authorization Service as defined in UA Part 12.

Profile.Name: Global Service KeyCredential Pull Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires providing the Information Model for Pull Management as defined in UA Part 12. For example KeyCredentials are needed to access an Authorization Service or a Broker. OPC UA Clients use this Information Model to request and update KeyCredentials they need.

Profile.Name: Global Service KeyCredential Push Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires the use of KeyCredential Push Management functions to set or update credentials in an OPC UA Server. For example KeyCredentials are needed to access an Authorization Service or a Broker. This OPC UA Server in turn has to provide the KeyCredentialConfigurationType Objects that represent required credentials.

Profile.Name: Historical Access Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read, process, and update historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Access Client Server Timestamp Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to request and process Server timestamps, in addition to source timestamps.

Profile.Name: Historical Access Modified Data 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support of reading modified historical values (values that where modified or inserted). This Facet supersedes the Historical Modified Data Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Access Modified Data Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to access prior historical data (values that were modified or inserted).

Profile.Name: Historical Access Structured Data 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet indicates that the Server supports storage and retrieval of structured values for all supported access types. If a listed access type is supported then the corresponding optional ConformanceUnit shall be supported. This Facet supersedes the Historical Access Structured Data Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Aggregate 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet indicates that the server supports aggregate processing to produce derived values from raw historical data. This Facet supersedes the Historical Aggregate Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Aggregate Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read historical data by specifying the needed aggregate. This implies consideration of the list of aggregates supported by the Server.

Profile.Name: Historical Annotation 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support for the storage and retrieval of annotations for historical data. This Facet supersedes the Historical Annotation Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Annotation Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to retrieve and write annotations for historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Data AtTime 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet indicates that the historical Server supports reading data by specifying specific timestamps. This Facet supersedes the Historical Data AtTime Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Data AtTime Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to access data at specific instances in time.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Delete 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Data Delete functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Data Delete Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Delete Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to delete historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Insert 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Data Insert functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Data Insert Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Insert Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to insert historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Replace 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Data Replace functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Data Replace Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Replace Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to replace historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Update 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Data Update functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Data Update Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Data Update Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to update historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Delete 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Event delete access functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Event Delete Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Delete Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to delete Historical events.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Insert 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Event insert access functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Event Insert Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Insert Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to insert historical events.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Replace 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Event replace access functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Event Replace Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Replace Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to replace historical events.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Update 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes Historical Event update access functionality. This Facet supersedes the Historical Event Update Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Event Update Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to update historical events.

Profile.Name: Historical Events Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read Historical Events, including simple filtering.

Profile.Name: Historical Raw Data 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the basic functionality when supporting historical data access for raw data. This Facet supersedes the Historical Raw Data Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Historical Structured Data Access Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read structured values for historical nodes.

Profile.Name: Historical Structured Data AtTime Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read structured values for historical nodes at specific instances in time.

Profile.Name: Historical Structured Data Delete Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to remove structured historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Structured Data Insert Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to insert structured historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Structured Data Modified Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to read structured values for prior historical data (values that were modified or inserted).

Profile.Name: Historical Structured Data Replace Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to replace structured historical data.

Profile.Name: Historical Structured Data Update Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to update structured historical data.

Profile.Name: Host Resolution Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the possible Host Resolution support options - i.e., the process through which an assigned hostname is converted or resolved to its mapped IP Address.

Profile.Name: HTTPS UA-Binary
Profile.Description: This transport Facet defines a combination of network protocol, security protocol and message encoding that balances compatibility with widely used HTTPS transport and a compact UA-Binary encoded message for added performance. It is expected that this transport will be used to support installations where firewalls only permit HTTPS or where a WEB browser is used as Client. This transport requires that one of the TransportSecurity Profiles for TLS be provided.

Profile.Name: HTTPS UA-JSON
Profile.Description: This transport Facet defines a combination of network protocol, security protocol and message encoding that uses HTTPS transport and a UA-JSON encoded message. This transport requires that one of the TransportSecurity Profiles for TLS be provided.

Profile.Name: HTTPS UA-XML
Profile.Description: This transport Facet defines a combination of network protocol, security protocol and message encoding that uses HTTPS transport and a SOAP XML encoded message for use with standard SOAP V1.2 toolkits. This transport requires that one of the TransportSecurity Profiles for TLS be provided.

Profile.Name: KeyCredential Service Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the capability to interact with a KeyCredential Service to obtain KeyCredentials. For example KeyCredentials are needed to access an Authorization Service or a Broker. The KeyCredential Service is typically part of a system-wide tool, like a GDS that also manages Applications, Access Tokens, and Certificates. The Facet also includes the ProfileUris representing the authentication mechanism used to communicate with the resource that accepts KeyCredentials.

Profile.Name: KeyCredential Service Server Facet
Profile.Description:
This Facet defines the capability of a Server to interact with a KeyCredential Service to obtain KeyCredentials. The Server provides the Information Model for Push Management specified as part of the KeyCredential Management in Part 12. The Facet also includes the ProfileUris representing the authentication mechanism used to communicate with the resource that accepts KeyCredentials.
For example KeyCredentials are needed to access an Authorization Service or a Broker. The KeyCredential Service is typically part of a system-wide tool, like a GDS that also manages Applications, Access Tokens, and Certificates.

Profile.Name: LogObject Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet supports the LogObject functionality - used to collect information, like diagnostic information. It is defined in UA Part 26.

Profile.Name: Method 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support of Method invocation via the Call service. Methods are “lightweight” functions which are similar to the methods of a class found in any object-oriented programming language. A Method can have its scope bounded by an owning Object or an owning ObjectType. Methods with an ObjectType as their scope are similar to static methods in a class.

Profile.Name: Method Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to call arbitrary Methods.

Profile.Name: Micro Embedded Device 2022 Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application specifically for small devices with limited resources. This Profile builds upon the Nano Embedded Device Server Profile. The most important additions is the support for subscriptions . A complete Type System is not required; however, if the Server implements any non-UA types then these types and their super-types shall be exposed.
This Profile supersedes the Micro Embedded Device 2017 Server Profile.

Profile.Name: Micro Embedded Device 2025 Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application specifically for small devices with limited resources. This Profile builds upon the Nano Embedded Device Server Profile. The most important additions is the support for subscriptions . A complete Type System is not required; however, if the Server implements any non-UA types then these types and their super-types shall be exposed.
This Profile supersedes the Micro Embedded Device 2022 Server Profile.

Profile.Name: Minimum UA 2025 Client Facet
Profile.Description:
This Profile defines the functionalities required for OPC UA Clients to establish and maintain Sessions through the OPC UA TCP binary protocol.
It supersedes the Minimum UA Client Facet making support for ECC policies optional.

Profile.Name: Minimum UA Client 2022 Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Client Application that defines the minimum set of functionalities required for certifiable OPC UA Clients. The Client shall provide connection establishment through the OPC UA TCP binary protocol with and without security.
This Profile supersedes the Minimum UA Client Profile.

Profile.Name: Minimum UA Client 2025 Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Client Application that defines the minimum set of functionalities required for certifiable OPC UA Clients. The Client shall provide connection establishment through the OPC UA TCP binary protocol with and without security.
This Profile supersedes the Minimum UA Client 2022 Profile.

Profile.Name: Minimum UA Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Profile defines the functionalities required for OPC UA Clients to establish and maintain Sessions through the OPC UA TCP binary protocol.

Profile.Name: Model Change Event Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support for ModelChangeEvents and the NodeVersion Property for Nodes. ModelChangeEvents are generated to indicate a change of the AddressSpace structure. The change may consist of adding or deleting a Node or Reference.

Profile.Name: Multi-Server Client Connection Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability for simultaneous access to multiple Servers.

Profile.Name: Nano Embedded Device 2022 Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application specifically for chip level devices with limited resources. This Profile is functionally equivalent to the Core Server Facet and defines the "UA-TCP UA-SC UA-Binary" as the required transport profile including an ECC Security Policy. The support of Diagnostic Objects and Variables is optional for this Profile despite it being defined as “mandatory” in UA Part 5. Support of Diagnostic Objects and Variables is mandatory in some higher-level Profiles. Exposing types in the AddressSpace is optional for this Profile except if custom types (i.e., types that are derived from well-known ObjectTypes, VariableTypes, ReferenceType or DataTypes) are used. Exposing all supported types in the AddressSpace is mandatory in some higher-level Profiles.
This Profile supersedes the Nano Embedded Device 2017 Server Profile.

Profile.Name: Nano Embedded Device 2025 Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application specifically for chip level devices with limited resources. This Profile is functionally equivalent to the Core Server Facet and defines the "UA-TCP UA-SC UA-Binary" as the required transport profile including optional ECC Security Policy. The support of Diagnostic Objects and Variables is optional for this Profile despite it being defined as “mandatory” in UA Part 5. Support of Diagnostic Objects and Variables is mandatory in some higher-level Profiles. Exposing types in the AddressSpace is optional for this Profile except if custom types (i.e., types that are derived from well-known ObjectTypes, VariableTypes, ReferenceType or DataTypes) are used. Exposing all supported types in the AddressSpace is mandatory in some higher-level Profiles.
This Profile supersedes the Nano Embedded Device 2022 Server Profile.

Profile.Name: Node Management 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires the support of the Services that allow the Client to add, modify and delete Nodes in the AddressSpace. These Services provide an interface which can be used to configure Servers. This means all changes to the AddressSpace are expected to persist even after the Client has disconnected from the Server. This Facet supersedes the Node Management Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Node Management Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to configure the AddressSpace of an OPC UA Server through OPC UA Node Management Service Set.

Profile.Name: Notifier and Source Hierarchy Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to find and use a hierarchy of Objects that are event notifier and Nodes that are event sources in the Server AddressSpace.

Profile.Name: Publisher Acyclic Limits Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes limits for acyclic sending of messages with complete or delta DataSets.

Profile.Name: Publisher Component Configuration Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Publisher supports the full range of configuration capabilities defined in UA Part 14. This includes the possibility to override individual parameters and the Methods for management of complete entities.

Profile.Name: Publisher Cyclic Limits Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes limits for sending messages in fixed cycles.

Profile.Name: Publisher Information Model Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Publisher is an OPC UA Server and exposes its configuration using the OPC UA PubSub Information Model.

Profile.Name: Publisher Message Security Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Publisher supports securing published messages. They may be signed and/or encrypted.

Profile.Name: Publisher Parameter Configuration Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Publisher can be configured from an OPC UA Client by writing to Variables in PubSub instances and changing the state with the Enable/Disable Methods.

Profile.Name: Publisher UADP Dynamic Data or Events Facet
Profile.Description: This is a Facet for a number of applications that allow grouping of multiple DataSets and where often only a subset or none of the DataSet fields will change during a cycle. The NetworkMessage header only identifies the Publisher and the contained DataSetMessages.

Profile.Name: Publisher UADP Flexible Layout Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability for a highly configurable publishing infrastructure. This includes the configuration of all entities, like published DataSets, DataSetWriters, WriterGroups, and Connections but also the header settings that determine which elements are to be included in messages.

Profile.Name: Publisher UADP Periodic Fixed Layout Facet
Profile.Description: This is a Facet with restricted functionality targeted to highly efficient, small footprint applications. The restrictions are set to allow periodic exchange of data with a static layout.

Profile.Name: Publisher UDP UADP Periodic Fixed 2022 Profile
Profile.Description:
This is a Publisher Profile targeted towards highly efficient encoding of UADP messages for periodic exchange of data with a static layout. This Profile is functionally equivalent to the UADP Periodic Facet and defines the PubSub UDP UADP protocol as the required transport profile.
This Profile assumes that datasets may change dynamically and therefore support for the corresponding ConformanceUnits is mandatory.
This Profile supersedes the Publisher UDP UADP Periodic Fixed Profile".

Profile.Name: Publisher UDP UADP Periodic Fixed StaticCfg Profile
Profile.Description: This is a Publisher Profile targeted towards highly efficient encoding of UADP messages for periodic exchange of data with a fixed layout. This Profile is functionally equivalent to the UADP Periodic Facet and defines the PubSub UDP UADP protocol as the required transport profile. It is assumed that Publishers and Subscribers are pre-configured and will not change dynamically.

Profile.Name: PubSub AMQP JSON
Profile.Description: This PubSub transport Facet defines a combination of the AMQP transport protocol mapping with JSON message mapping. This Facet is used for broker-based messaging.

Profile.Name: PubSub AMQP UADP
Profile.Description: This PubSub transport Facet defines a combination of the AMQP transport protocol mapping with UADP message mapping. This Facet is used for broker-based messaging.

Profile.Name: PubSub MQTT JSON
Profile.Description: This PubSub transport Facet defines a combination of the MQTT transport protocol mapping with JSON message mapping. This Facet is used for broker-based messaging.

Profile.Name: PubSub MQTT UADP
Profile.Description: This PubSub transport Facet defines a combination of the MQTT transport protocol mapping with UADP message mapping. This Facet is used for broker-based messaging.

Profile.Name: PubSub UDP UADP
Profile.Description: This PubSub transport Facet defines a combination of the UDP transport protocol mapping with UADP message mapping. This Facet is used for broker-less messaging.

Profile.Name: PubSub UDP UADP DTLS
Profile.Description: This PubSub Transport Facet defines the PubSub UDP UADP Profile with support for DTLS transport security, and the GDS certificate manager for managing the certificates.

Profile.Name: Redundancy Switch Client Facet
Profile.Description: A Client that supports this Facet supports monitoring the redundancy status for non-transparent redundant Servers and switching to the backup Server when they recognize a change.

Profile.Name: Redundancy Transparent Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires support for transparent redundancy. If Servers implement transparent redundancy then the failover from one Server to another is transparent to the Client such that the Client is unaware that a failover has occurred; the Client is not required to do anything at all to keep data flowing. This type of redundancy is usually a hardware solution.

Profile.Name: Redundancy Visible Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support for non-transparent redundancy. Failover for this type of redundancy requires the Client to monitor Server status and to switch to a backup Server if it detects a failure. The Server shall expose the methods of failover it supports (cold, warm or hot). The failover method tells the Client what it shall do when connecting to a Server and when a failure occurs. Cold redundancy requires a Client to reconnect to a backup Server after the initial Server has failed. Warm redundancy allows a Client to connect to multiple Servers, but only one Server will be providing values. In hot redundancy multiple Servers are able to provide data and a Client can connect to multiple Servers for the data.

Profile.Name: Redundant Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use the redundancy feature available for redundant Clients.

Profile.Name: Request State Change Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the ability to invoke the RequestServerStateChange Method.

Profile.Name: Request State Change Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support of the RequestServerStateChange Method.

Profile.Name: Reverse Connect Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support of reverse connectivity in a Client. Usually, a connection is opened by the Client before starting the UA-specific handshake. This will fail, however, when Servers are behind firewalls. In the reverse connectivity scenario, the Client accepts a connection request and a ReverseHello message from a Server and establishes a Secure Channel using this connection.

Profile.Name: Reverse Connect Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support of reverse connectivity in a Server. Usually, a connection is opened by the Client before starting the UA-specific handshake. This will fail, however, when Servers are behind firewalls with no open ports to connect to. In the reverse connectivity scenario, the Server opens the connection and starts with a ReverseHello message requesting that the Client establish a Secure Channel using this connection.

Profile.Name: SafetyAutomationComponent Facet
Profile.Description: Describes communication partners in a unidirectional safety link. A SafetyAutomationComponent can be a SafetyProvider (data source), a SafetyConsumer (data sink), or both.

Profile.Name: SafetyConsumer Facet
Profile.Description: Describes a SafetyConsumer, which is the data sink of a unidirectional safety link.

Profile.Name: SafetyConsumerClient Facet
Profile.Description: Describes a SafetyConsumer which consumes data via Client/Server mechanisms.

Profile.Name: SafetyConsumerPubSub Facet
Profile.Description: Describes a SafetyConsumer which consumes data via PubSub mechanisms.

Profile.Name: SafetyConsumerPubSubMapper Facet
Profile.Description: Describes how a SafetyConsumer requests and receives data from a SafetyProvider using PubSub.

Profile.Name: SafetyProvider Facet
Profile.Description: Describes a SafetyProvider, which is the data source of a unidirectional safety link.

Profile.Name: SafetyProviderPubSub Facet
Profile.Description: Describes a SafetyProvider which provides its data via PubSub mechanisms.

Profile.Name: SafetyProviderPubSubMapper Facet
Profile.Description: Describes how a Safety provider provides its data using PubSub.

Profile.Name: SafetyProviderServer Facet
Profile.Description: Describes a SafetyProvider which provides its data via Client/Server mechanisms.

Profile.Name: SafetyProviderServerMapper Facet
Profile.Description: Describes how a SafetyProvider provides its data and diagnostic information using OPC UA Methods.

Profile.Name: Scheduler Base Server Facet
Profile.Description: A Facet that describes the base characteristics for OPC UA Servers that support exposing schedules.

Profile.Name: Scheduler Configuration Client Facet
Profile.Description: A Facet that describes the base characteristics for all OPC UA Clients that support the configuration of schedules.

Profile.Name: Scheduler Configuration Server Facet
Profile.Description: A Facet that describes the base characteristics for OPC UA Servers that support configuring schedules.

Profile.Name: Security Time Synchronization
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the possible time synchronization options required for OPC UA Security.

Profile.Name: Security User Access Control Base
Profile.Description: This Facet defines basic support for access restrictions to certain validated users. [Note: In the future this facet will be Deprecated and replaced by "Security User Access Control Base 2023 Server"]

Profile.Name: Security User Access Control Base Server 2023
Profile.Description: This Facet defines basic Server support for access restrictions to certain validated users. It is recommended that multiple manners of identifying users is provided.

Profile.Name: Security User Access Control Full
Profile.Description: This Facet defines advanced support for access restrictions to certain validated users. [Note: in the Future this Facet will be Deprecated and replaced by "Security User Access Control Full Server 2023"]

Profile.Name: Security User Access Control Full Server 2023
Profile.Description: This Facet defines advanced support for access restrictions to certain validated users.

Profile.Name: SecurityPolicy - Aes256-Sha256-RsaPss
Profile.Description:
This security Facet defines a security policy for configurations with a need for high security. It requires a PKI infrastructure.
This SecurityPolicy has LegacySequenceNumbers set to TRUE. This refers to sequence number handling rules described in UA Part 6.
As computing power increases, security policies are expected to expire. NIST provides guidelines for expected expiration dates for individual algorithms. These guidelines provide recommended dates at which the algorithm should be replaced or upgraded to a more secure algorithm. They do not indicate a failure of the algorithm. This security policy has no published end dates as of this time.
It is recommended that Servers and Clients support all security profiles and support configurability of actual exposed and default security policies.

Profile.Name: SecurityPolicy - PubSub-Aes256-CTR
Profile.Description: This PubSub security Facet defines the set of algorithms and key lengths used for UADP message mapping. It is a security policy for configurations with high security needs.

Profile.Name: SecurityPolicy - RSA-DH-AesGcm
Profile.Description:
This security profile facet requires RSA keys with the Diffie-Hellmen (DH) algorithm used to negotiate the shared secret.
It also uses AES-GCM for symmetric encryption which is preferable to AES-CBC. This profile facet is generally better than the existing RSA profile facets and can replace them.

This security policy has no published end dates as of this time.

2) Documentation shall describe that it should not be used.
3) It will still be tested to ensure correct operation.

Profile.Name: Standard 2022 UA Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application for devices like a PC.
This Profile supersedes the Standard 2017 UA Server Profile.

Profile.Name: Standard 2025 UA Server Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Server Application for devices like a PC.

Profile.Name: Standard DataChange Subscription 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the standard support of subscribing to data changes and extends features defined by the Embedded Data Change Subscription 2021 Facet. Note that the Method Call Service is only required for the Methods defined in this Facet. This Facet supersedes the Standard DataChange Subscription 2017 Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Standard Event Subscription 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the standard support for subscribing to events. Support of this Facet requires the implementation of Event Types representing the Events that the Server can report and their specific fields. This Facet supersedes the Standard Event Subscription Server Facet.

Profile.Name: Standard UA Client 2022 Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Client Application that defines a set of functionality required for generic OPC UA Clients. Such a Client shall be able to use local, subnet and global discovery. It shall be able to maintain a connection with a single Session (as required for nano embedded Servers). If Subscriptions are used, the Client shall respect the limits of Servers with limited resources. If a Server does not support Subscriptions, the Client shall provide read access as fallback. The Client shall provide connection establishment through the OPC UA TCP binary protocol with and without security.
This Profile supersedes the Standard UA Client 2017 Profile,

Profile.Name: Standard UA Client 2025 Profile
Profile.Description:
This Profile is a collection of Facets necessary to build a functional OPC UA Client Application that defines a set of functionality required for generic OPC UA Clients. Such a Client shall be able to use local, subnet and global discovery. It shall be able to maintain a connection with a single Session (as required for nano embedded Servers). If Subscriptions are used, the Client shall respect the limits of Servers with limited resources. If a Server does not support Subscriptions, the Client shall provide read access as fallback. The Client shall provide connection establishment through the OPC UA TCP binary protocol with and without security.

Profile.Name: State Machine 2022 Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support of StateMachines based on the types in UA Part "State Machines". This Facet supersedes the State Machine Server Facet.

Profile.Name: State Machine Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use state machines based on the StateMachineType or a sub-type.

Profile.Name: Subnet Discovery Client Facet
Profile.Description: Support of this Facet enables discovery of the Server on a subnet.

Profile.Name: Subnet Discovery Server Facet
Profile.Description: Support of this Facet enables discovery of the Server on a subnet using mDNS. This Facet is typically only implemented in Servers that do not register with an LDS.

Profile.Name: Subscriber Acyclic Limits Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes limits for receiving acyclically sent messages with complete or delta DataSets.

Profile.Name: Subscriber Component Configuration Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Subscriber supports the full range of configuration capabilities defined in UA Part 14. This includes the possibility to override individual parameters and the Methods for management of complete entities.

Profile.Name: Subscriber Cyclic Limits Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet includes limits for receiving messages in fixed cycles.

Profile.Name: Subscriber Information Model Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Subscriber is an OPC UA Server and exposes its configuration using the OPC UA PubSub Information Model.

Profile.Name: Subscriber Message Security Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Subscriber can deal with messages that are signed and/or encrypted.

Profile.Name: Subscriber Parameter Configuration Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet requires that the Subscriber can be configured from an OPC UA Client by writing to Variables in PubSub instances and the state can be set using the Enable/Disable Methods.

Profile.Name: Subscriber UADP Dynamic Data or Events Facet
Profile.Description: This is a Facet for use cases where the number and ordering of DataSetMessages within NetworkMessages can change arbitrarily and where often only a subset or none of the DataSet fields will change during a cycle.

Profile.Name: Subscriber UADP Flexible Layout Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support of processing customizable UADP messages.

Profile.Name: Subscriber UADP Periodic Fixed Layout Facet
Profile.Description: This is a restricted Facet targeted to high efficient, small footprint applications. The restrictions are set to allow periodic exchange of data with a static layout.

Profile.Name: Subscriber UDP UADP Periodic Fixed 2022 Profile
Profile.Description:
This is a Subscriber Profile targeted towards highly efficient decoding of UADP messages for periodic exchange of data with a static layout. This Profile is functionally equivalent to the UADP Periodic Facet and defines the PubSub UDP UADP protocol as the required transport profile.
This Profile assumes that datasets may change dynamically and therefore support for the corresponding ConformanceUnits is mandatory.

This Profile supersedes the Subscriber UDP UADP Periodic Fixed Profile".

Profile.Name: Subscriber UDP UADP Periodic Fixed StaticCfg Profile
Profile.Description:
This is a Subscriber Profile targeted towards highly efficient decoding of UADP messages for periodic exchange of data with a static layout. This Profile is functionally equivalent to the UADP Periodic Facet and defines the PubSub UDP UADP protocol as the required transport profile.
It is assumed that Publishers and Subscribers are pre-configured and will not change dynamically.

Profile.Name: Temporary File Access Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the use of temporary files. This includes creating such files and one of the defined access forms.

Profile.Name: Temporary File Access Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet specifies the support of creating and accessing temporary files. This includes one of the defined access forms.

Profile.Name: TransportSecurity – TLS 1.0
Profile.Description:
Note: This Transport Security has been deprecated with the OPC UA Specification Version 1.03.

This Facet defines a transport security for configurations with medium high security needs. It makes uses of TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA. This security profile is less secure than TLS 1.2. As computing power increases, security algorithms are expected to expire. NIST provides guidelines for expected expiration dates for individual algorithms. These guidelines provide recommended dates at which the algorithm should be replaced or upgraded to a more secure algorithm. They do not indicate a failure of the algorithm. NIST already recommends users of this TransportSecurity should upgrade to TLS 1.2. This Policy is listed for systems that do not support TLS 1.1 or 1.2. It is recommended that Servers and Clients support all security profiles and developers provide the recommended profile as a default. It is up to an administrator to configure the actual exposed TransportSecurity Profiles.

Profile.Name: TransportSecurity – TLS 1.1
Profile.Description:
Note: This Transport Security has been deprecated with the OPC UA Specification Version 1.03.

This Facet defines a transport security for configurations with medium high security needs. This security profile is less secure than TLS 1.2. As computing power increases, security algorithms are expected to expire. NIST provides guidelines for expected expiration dates for individual algorithms. These guidelines provided recommended dates at which the algorithm should be replaced or upgraded to a more secure algorithm. They do not indicate a failure of the algorithm. NIST recommends users of this TransportSecurity should consider upgrading to TLS 1.2. This transport security is provided for systems that do not support TLS 1.2. It is recommended that Servers and Clients support all security profiles and developers provide the recommended profile as a default. It is up to an administrator to configure the actual exposed TransportSecurity Profiles.

Profile.Name: TransportSecurity – TLS 1.2
Profile.Description: This Facet defines a transport security for configurations with high security needs. It makes use of TLS 1.2 and uses TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA256. As computing power increases, security algorithms are expected to expire. NIST provides guidelines for expected expiration dates for individual algorithms. These guidelines provide recommended dates at which the algorithm should be replaced or upgraded to a more secure algorithm. They do not indicate a failure of the algorithm. NIST has no recommendations for this TransportSecurity. It is recommended that Servers and Clients support all security profiles and developers provide the recommended profile as a default. It is up to an administrator to configure the actual exposed TransportSecurity Profiles.

Profile.Name: TransportSecurity – TLS 1.2 with PFS
Profile.Description:
This Facet defines a transport security for configurations with high security needs and perfect forward secrecy (PFS). It makes use of TLS 1.2 and uses TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256 or TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA256.
As computing power increases, security algorithms are expected to expire. NIST provides guidelines for expected expiration dates for individual algorithms. These guidelines provide recommended dates at which the algorithm should be replaced or upgraded to a more secure algorithm. They do not indicate a failure of the algorithm. NIST has no recommendations for this TransportSecurity. It is recommended that Servers and Clients support all security profiles and developers provide the recommended profile as a default. It is up to an administrator to configure the actual exposed TransportSecurity Profiles.

Profile.Name: UA-TCP UA-SC UA-Binary

Profile.Name: User Token – Anonymous Facet

Profile.Name: User Token – Issued Token Windows Server Facet

This User Token has been deprecated with OPC UA Specification Version 1.05.
This Facet further refines the User Token - Issued Token to indicate a windows implementation of Kerberos

Profile.Name: User Token – JWT Client Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines the ability to use JSON Web Tokens (JWT) as user identification during Session setup. JWTs are used to request an access token from an external Authorization Service.

Profile.Name: User Token – JWT Server Facet
Profile.Description: This Facet defines support for JSON Web Tokens (JWT) to identify the user during Session setup. A JWT is the Access Token format which OPC UA requires when using OAuth2.

Profile.Name: User Token – User Name Password Client Facet

Profile.Name: User Token – User Name Password Server Facet

ConformanceUnit.Name: Address Space NonVolatile and Constant

ConformanceUnit.Name: Address Space UserWriteMask Multilevel

ConformanceUnit.Name: AsymmetricEncryptionAlgorithm_None
ConformanceUnit.Description: This algorithm does not apply.

ConformanceUnit.Name: AsymmetricEncryptionAlgorithm_RSA-OAEP-SHA1
ConformanceUnit.Description: The RSA encryption algorithm which is defined in https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3447. The RSAES-OAEP scheme is used. The hash algorithm is SHA1 and is described in https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6234. The mask generation algorithm also uses SHA1. The URI is http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#rsa-oaep. No known exploits exist when using SHA1 with RSAES-OAEP, however, SHA1 was broken in 2017 so use of this algorithm is not recommended.

ConformanceUnit.Name: AsymmetricEncryptionAlgorithm_RSA-OAEP-SHA2-256

The hash algorithm is SHA2 with 256 bits and is described in https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6234. The mask generation algorithm also uses SHA2 with 256 bits. The URI is http://opcfoundation.org/UA/security/rsa-oaep-sha2-256.

ConformanceUnit.Name: AsymmetricEncryptionAlgorithm_RSA-PKCS15

ConformanceUnit.Name: AsymmetricSignatureAlgorithm_ECDSA-SHA2-384

ConformanceUnit.Name: AsymmetricSignatureAlgorithm_None

ConformanceUnit.Name: AsymmetricSignatureAlgorithm_RSA-PKCS15-SHA2-256
